title: American Time Use Survey sleeping aggregate series mirrored by DBnomics
publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics via DBnomics

doi.absence_reason: The BLS LABSTAT aggregate series and DBnomics dataset snapshot do not assign a DOI.

license.name: DBnomics open database terms with underlying U.S. BLS public-data terms

measurement_uncertainty.description: The mirrored series response used here does not expose standard errors, respondent weights, or diary-level sampling uncertainty.

known_gaps: The accessible mirror contains aggregate LABSTAT series rather than respondent-level ATUS diary microdata.
The mirror snapshot supplies values through 2023 and does not include the BLS 2024 release.
Official BLS 2024 microdata ZIP requests returned an automated-access denial in this execution environment, so no denied response is registered as source data.
Aggregate means cannot establish within-person event frequency, duration, start-time, transition, or between-person distributions.
The 2023 all-person sleeping estimate is used only as an untouched plausibility screen for a deterministic object-runner output.
The array engine is excluded because its fixed-duration sleep execution is not yet conformant with the object engine.

preprocessing.description: Verify one DBnomics snapshot, select the BLS all-person sleeping series and matched age/sex strata, reserve 2023 as an untouched aggregate holdout, run the production object engine for 30 deterministic days, and compare simulated daily sleep with the frozen 30-minute error limit.

permitted_use.purpose: Aggregate occupant-behavior plausibility screening and validation-tool verification
permitted_use.notes: Attribute BLS as the underlying provider and DBnomics as the access path. Do not present aggregate estimates as diary microdata or evidence of individual distributions.
